chunks: And the wergild (blood money) for the wrist, when it is bruised so that it is bandaged upon and there is no fault or defect, is one-third of the wergild of the hand, being one hundred and sixty-six Dinars, and one-third of a Dinar.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a bruised wrist in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the precise monetary valuation for *rusg* (wrist) injuries, distinguishing between temporary bruising and permanent defects. The calculation of 166 and two-thirds Dinars reflects the classical standard where the hand's total *diyah* is 500 Dinars, illustrating the systematic approach to bodily compensation in *fiqh al-ayah*. This specific ruling underscores the importance of distinguishing between transient injuries and those causing lasting impairment in legal judgments.
